A test of what a reader keeps as it condenses a document

Source: R/doc-bench-condense.R
gr_condensation_check.Rd

Builds a benchmark for hr_benchmark(): documents with planted facts, lures and a later correction, read forwards and reversed, with one question per fact and a scorer that needs no model. Arms that differ in how they carry a document (a gr_read_spec() refine_state, a context_policy, a reader) are run on its reference and scored with its scorer; gr_condensation_summary() reads the result.

Usage

gr_condensation_check(
  text = NULL,
  n_facts = 6L,
  n_lures = 2L,
  correction = TRUE,
  n_documents = 1L,
  paragraphs = 12L,
  orders = c("forward", "reversed"),
  seed = 1L,
  split = "test"
)

# S3 method for class 'gr_condensation_check'
print(x, ...)

gr_condensation_summary(check, bench)

Arguments

text

NULL for synthetic documents, or a document of your own as one string, whose paragraphs (split at blank lines) the facts are planted between. Its own text must not mention the planted places.

n_facts

Facts per document, 2 to 10.

n_lures

How many of the facts get a lure, 0 to n_facts - 1.

correction

Whether the last fact is stated wrongly early and corrected late.

n_documents

Synthetic documents to build, each its own cluster; 1 when text is given. A document's forward and reversed copies carry the same facts, so they share its cluster.

paragraphs

Filler paragraphs per synthetic document, at least n_facts.

orders

"forward", "reversed" or both.

seed

A whole number that fixes the places and values.

split

The split of every item; see hr_reference().

x

A gr_condensation_check.

...

Ignored.

check

A gr_condensation_check.

bench

An hr_benchmark() result on check$reference.

Value

gr_condensation_check() returns an object of class gr_condensation_check, a list of reference (an hr_reference() whose payloads are question and document, as gr_qa_reference() builds them), scorer (an hr_scorer() named "condensation"), items (a data frame of item, document, order, kind ("fact", "lure" or "correction"), position (where the fact sits in the forward document, from 0 at the start to 1 at the end), question, answer, lure and superseded) and documents (the texts, named by document and order).

gr_condensation_summary() returns a data frame with one row per arm and order: fact_recall (the share of runs whose answer holds the fact's value, over every item), lure_rate (the share of runs on lure items whose answer holds the lure's value), correction_won (the share of runs on correction items that are right), late_recall (fact recall over the facts in the last third of the document as it was read) and runs.

Details

Each document is a run of plain paragraphs, from text or from neutral filler sentences, with n_facts facts planted at evenly spread positions from the first paragraph to the last: "The budget of the Harbour depot was 41.3 million dollars." Each fact gets a question whose answer is its value. For the first n_lures facts a lure is planted as well, the same measure for a near-namesake ("the Harbour depot annexe") with another value. With correction = TRUE, the last fact is first stated with a wrong value in the opening paragraphs and corrected near the end ("Correction: ... was 248. The figure of 212 given earlier was wrong."). Every document is then given forwards and reversed by paragraph (gr_reverse_text()), so a fact near the end for one order is near the start for the other.

The values are fixed by seed with arithmetic, not by the random number generator, so the same call builds the same benchmark in any session.

The scorer finds the values in the answer as gr_scorer_answer() finds an answer: folded, and as a whole number. A fact item is right when the answer holds its value. A lure item is right when it holds the value and not the lure's. A correction item is right when it holds the corrected value and not the superseded one. The outcome names what was found: "answer", "lure", "superseded", "answer+lure", "answer+superseded", "not_found" or "other".

See also

gr_reverse_text(), hr_benchmark(), gr_arm(), gr_read_spec() for refine_state and context_policy

Examples

chk <- gr_condensation_check(n_facts = 4, n_lures = 1)
chk
#> <gr_condensation_check> 1 document(s), forward and reversed, 8 item(s)
#>   per order: 2 fact, 1 lure, 1 correction
head(chk$items[, c("item", "kind", "question", "answer", "lure")])
#>                     item       kind
#> 1       d1.lure1.forward       lure
#> 2       d1.fact2.forward       fact
#> 3       d1.fact3.forward       fact
#> 4 d1.correction4.forward correction
#> 5      d1.lure1.reversed       lure
#> 6      d1.fact2.reversed       fact
#>                                                question answer  lure
#> 1      What was the floor area of the Northgate clinic?  3,565 4,120
#> 2 How many yearly visits did the Riverside school have? 10,237  <NA>
#> 3        What was the budget of the Elm Street library?   42.5  <NA>
#> 4       What was the staff count of the Westfield mill?    321  <NA>
#> 5      What was the floor area of the Northgate clinic?  3,565 4,120
#> 6 How many yearly visits did the Riverside school have? 10,237  <NA>

# Two arms that differ only in what refine carries, on a stand-in model
# that answers every question with the planted budget.
cl <- gr_mock_client(function(m, p) {
  if (grepl("Reply with the edits", m[[length(m)]]$content, fixed = TRUE)) return("NONE")
  "The budget was 41.3 million dollars."
})
arms <- hr_sweep(gr_arm("thorough", list(reader = "refine", method = "paragraph")),
                 list(refine_state = c("draft", "ledger")))
bench <- suppressWarnings(hr_benchmark(arms, chk$reference, runs = 1, client = cl,
                                       scorer = chk$scorer))
